items.title: Residual Shunt at 6 Months Follow-up After Percutaneous Patent Foramen Ovale Closure in CAHAL: A Comparison of Occlutech and Amplatzer.
items.abstract: Residual shunt is a known complication in percutaneous patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure, and moderate to large residual shunt has been associated with an increased risk of recurrent stroke. Device-related factors, such as device size, have been associated with residual shunt, but comparative data per device type are scarce. We compared the prevalence of moderate to large residual shunt at 6 months between the Amplatzer and Occlutech devices. In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing successful percutaneous PFO closure with an Amplatzer or Occlutech dedicated closure device within the CAHAL centers Amsterdam UMC and Leiden UMC between 2018 and 2024 were included. The study population was divided into patients treated with an Occlutech and an Amplatzer device. The prevalence of moderate/large residual shunt at 6 months of follow-up was compared between the two groups. As a sensitivity analysis, a logistic regression was conducted to determine the association between the treatment groups and moderate/large residual shunt. The logistic regression was conducted in a weighted population using inverse probability weighting (IPTW), correcting for age, sex, smoking status, shunt size at baseline, device size, and atrial septal aneurysm. A total of 413 patients were included with an average age of 45.8 ± 11.3 years and 51.6% were male. Of the included patients, 279 were treated with an Amplatzer- and 134 with an Occlutech device. In the group treated with an Amplatzer, 22.2% of the patients had a moderate or large residual shunt at 6 months compared to 14.9% in the Occlutech group (p = 0.11). The sensitivity analysis did not show an association between device type and moderate/large shunt OR 0.71 (95% CI: 0.39-1.28, p = 0.25). In this study, no significant difference was observed in moderate/large residual shunt prevalence at 6 months of follow-up between the Occlutech and Amplatzer devices.

items.title: Variation in Anticoagulation Practice for Atrial High-Rate Episodes: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey.
items.abstract: Atrial high-rate episodes (AHRE) detected by cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) are associated with increased thromboembolic risk, yet their clinical significance and optimal anticoagulation strategy remain uncertain, particularly in the absence of electrocardiogram (ECG)-confirmed atrial fibrillation. We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey of UK clinicians involved in CIED follow-up. The survey assessed anticoagulation decision-making in AHRE, including episode-duration thresholds, cumulative burden, CHA 2 DS 2 -VA use, additional ECG monitoring, and anticoagulant choice. Only responses from UK-based consultant clinicians were included and analysed descriptively. A total of 51 responses were received; 38 met the inclusion criteria and were analysed. Most respondents (86.8%) reported having reviewed AHRE alerts within the preceding 6 months, indicating that AHRE are commonly encountered in clinical practice. A ≥ 24-h episode was the most common threshold for anticoagulation (44.7%), although many clinicians reported lower thresholds or individualised approaches. Nearly half (44.7%) did not consider cumulative AHRE burden in decision-making. CHA 2 DS 2 -VA thresholds also varied, most commonly ≥ 2 or ≥ 1. Additional ECG monitoring was infrequently performed. Direct oral anticoagulants were universally preferred, with apixaban the most commonly selected agent (73.7%). There is substantial variation in UK clinical practice regarding anticoagulation for AHRE, reflecting ongoing uncertainty and lack of clear guidance. These findings highlight the need for evidence-based thresholds to support consistent and informed clinical decision-making.

items.title: Electrophysiological Characteristics of Fasciculoventricular Pathways.
items.abstract: Fasciculoventricular (FV) accessory pathways are rare variants of pre-excitation, connecting the His-Purkinje system to ventricular myocardium. Though typically benign and not participating in tachycardia circuits, they can mimic septal accessory pathways on ECG, creating diagnostic challenges. To assess the prevalence, ECG characteristics, electrophysiological features, and atypical properties of FV pathways in patients undergoing EP study at a tertiary center. This retrospective observational study analyzed all patients undergoing EP study from 2010 to 2024. FV pathways were diagnosed by subtle pre-excitation, short and fixed HV interval, and lack of change in pre-excitation during atrial pacing. Of 2836 patients undergoing EP study for supraventricular tachycardia, 668 had accessory pathways; 15 (2.2%) had FV pathways. The mean age was 26.5 years, with 53% male. Four patients (27%) were asymptomatic. Coexisting arrhythmias included AV accessory pathways (40%), AVNRT (20%), and atrial arrhythmias (15%). All patients showed subtle pre-excitation (mean PR 101 ± 18.7 ms, QRS 105 ± 14.4 ms). EP study revealed a short fixed HV interval (mean 17.6 ± 5.85 ms) with persistent pre-excitation during atrial pacing. Atypical features included intermittent FV conduction (13%), gap phenomenon (7%), and retrograde conduction (20%). FV pathways were not involved in any tachycardia circuit. FV pathways are uncommon (2.2% of accessory pathways) with characteristic ECG and EP findings. The presence of gap phenomenon, intermittent antegrade conduction, and retrograde conduction suggests that a subset of these pathways may possess functional, discrete myocardial properties rather than passive insulation defects; however, further structural and electroanatomical studies are needed to confirm this hypothesis.

items.title: Serum sclerostin in relation to insulin resistance and epicardial fat thickness in obese women.
items.abstract: Visceral obesity is closely linked to insulin resistance and cardiometabolic risk. Epicardial adipose tissue, commonly assessed by epicardial fat thickness (EFT), is a clinically relevant fat depot associated with early cardiac remodelling. Sclerostin, a bone-derived protein, may play a role in crosstalk between the skeleton and adipose tissue. However, its relationship with insulin resistance and cardiac visceral fat remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate serum sclerostin levels and their association with insulin resistance and EFT in obese women. This case-control study included 90 women (55 obese and 35 age-matched controls). Participants underwent anthropometric and metabolic assessment, including serum sclerostin measurement. Insulin resistance was evaluated using HOMA-IR, and EFT was assessed by echocardiography. Correlation, ROC, and regression analyses were performed. Serum sclerostin levels were significantly higher in obese women than in controls (p<0.001). Sclerostin was positively correlated with fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and EFT. Levels were higher in insulin-resistant obese participants than in metabolically healthier obese individuals. ROC analysis showed good discriminative ability for insulin resistance (AUC=0.89) and moderate accuracy for identifying increased EFT (AUC=0.80). In multivariate analysis, BMI, but not sclerostin, remained an independent predictor of increased EFT. Serum sclerostin is elevated in obese women and is associated with insulin resistance and adverse metabolic profiles. Although not independently associated with epicardial fat thickness, it reflects metabolic dysfunction related to visceral adiposity and may serve as an indicator of metabolically unhealthy obesity within this cohort.

items.title: Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of the left atrium in daily practice: a practical guide.
items.abstract: The left atrium (LA) is a crucial component of cardiovascular performance. A thorough understanding of LA anatomy, physiology, and pathology is necessary for diagnostic and prognostic purposes in daily clinical practice. LA volume is widely recognized as a novel biomarker for cardiovascular risks in the general population. Furthermore, it has been shown to be a significant prognostic factor in various cardiac conditions, such as atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, valvular heart disease, and heart failure. The assessment of LA function in physiologic and pathologic states has gathered interest with expanding research supporting its utility as a biomarker for outcomes in different cardiovascular abnormalities. Utilizing basic and advanced echocardiographic modalities and integrating multiple parameters helps in both qualitative and quantitative assessment of LA size and function. This is a narrative review provides a comprehensive approach to assessing LA size and function by interpreting existing English-language literature, including landmark studies, reviews and consensus documents from leading echocardiography societies. The literature search focused on key terms, such as LA size, phasic function, strain, and Doppler hemodynamics. By collecting, analyzing, and grouping the echocardiographic parameters, we introduce a simplified approach to guide clinicians through a comprehensive LA assessment ranging from standard 2D dimensions to advanced deformational tracking tailored to specific clinical indications.

items.title: Conversion Surgery After HAIC-Based Combination Therapy with Targeted Therapy and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors for Initially Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: For selected patients whose initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) responds to hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC)-based combination treatment, conversion surgery may provide an opportunity for curative-intent management. We quantified the frequency of conversion surgery, examined factors associated with surgical conversion, and assessed survival and pathological outcomes using analyses that accounted for immortal time bias. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 216 patients with initially unresectable HCC who received HAIC together with targeted therapy and immune checkpoint blockade from September 2020 through June 2023. The relationship between conversion surgery and survival was examined with time-dependent Cox regression and a prespecified 180-day landmark analysis. Two hepatopathologists independently assessed the pathological response. 47 (21.8%) patients underwent conversion surgery, and 16 (34.0%) achieved pathological complete response (pCR). Median overall survival (OS) was 22.7 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 21.1-25.8), and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 13.7 months (95% CI, 10.9-16.2). In adjusted 180-day landmark analyses including 211 patients for OS and 166 patients for PFS, conversion surgery was associated with lower hazards of death (hazard ratio [HR], 0.30; 95% CI, 0.16-0.59; P P = 0.001); time-dependent Cox models produced consistent findings. Albumin ≥ 35 g/L was associated with higher odds of conversion surgery (odds ratio [OR], 5.47; 95% CI, 1.75-17.06), whereas multifocal tumors were associated with lower odds (OR, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.06-0.29). Among resected patients, pCR was associated with favorable postoperative outcomes in exploratory unadjusted analyses. 47 of 216 patients (21.8%) underwent conversion surgery after HAIC-based combination therapy. Conversion surgery was associated with favorable OS and PFS after accounting for treatment timing. However, causal inference remains limited by residual confounding and treatment-selection bias in this retrospective study. The prognostic value of pCR requires validation in larger prospective cohorts. Some patients with liver cancer cannot undergo surgery when first diagnosed. In this study, we reviewed 216 patients who received chemotherapy through the liver’s artery together with targeted therapy and immunotherapy. After treatment and review by a team of specialists, about one in five patients underwent liver resection. Patients who underwent conversion surgery tended to live longer and remain free from disease progression for longer. The analyses accounted for the time patients needed to become eligible for surgery. Because this study looked back at patients’ medical records, the results should be interpreted with caution and need confirmation in future studies. In about one-third of patients who underwent surgery, doctors found no remaining viable cancer cells when they examined the removed tumors. These patients had favorable postoperative outcomes, but the small number of outcome events means that this finding requires confirmation in larger studies.

items.title: Early Assessment of Circulating Tumor Cells and Their PD-L1 Expression as Predictive Biomarkers in Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients Treated with Immunotherapy: An Exploratory Study.
items.abstract: The prognosis of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC) has improved in recent years but therapeutic benefit remains heterogeneous, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers. Liquid biopsy techniques, including the analysis of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression on CTCs (PD-L1-CTCs), have emerged as promising tools. We conducted a retrospective study in a cohort of mNSCLC patients treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs) to evaluate the predictive value of these biomarkers at baseline and at an early time point during treatment. CTCs were captured with the ClearCell ® FX platform and then assessed for PD-L1 by immunostaining. Therapeutic drug monitoring of nivolumab and pembrolizumab was performed. Thirty-seven mNSCLC patients were enrolled. The median CTCs count was 35 CTCs per 7.5 mL of whole blood (standard deviation ± 939). PD-L1-CTCs were detected in 51% of patients. No correlation was found between PD-L1-CTCs and PD-L1 on tumor Formalin-Fixed, Paraffin-Embedded (FFPE) tissue. Higher-than-median CTCs count was associated with a trend toward worse outcomes. In contrast, PD-L1 expression on CTCs did not predict treatment response. Most patients presented a trough concentration of ICI at cure 3 above 10 µg/mL, regardless clinical response. Baseline CTCs levels tended to be associated with clinical outcomes, whereas PD-L1 expression on CTCs was not. Early evaluation of changes in these two parameters did not improve outcome prediction under ICI treatment. Larger studies with longer follow-up and more in-depth analyses are warranted to further define the prognostic and predictive value of CTC-based biomarkers.

items.title: Protein Lactylation in Cancer: From Mechanisms to Therapy.
items.abstract: Protein lactylation has emerged as a metabolically responsive posttranslational modification linking lactate accumulation to epigenetic and functional adaptation in cancer. Initially identified on histones, lactylation is now recognized on diverse nonhistone proteins involved in DNA damage repair, immune regulation, redox homeostasis, metabolic remodeling, and cellular plasticity. However, current evidence remains fragmented across treatment modalities, and many reported lactylation events lack site-specific functional validation and translational assessment. This review addresses this gap by integrating the metabolic and enzymatic basis of protein lactylation with its roles in chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. We critically examine how lactylation may promote tumor persistence under therapeutic pressure by enhancing genome maintenance, immune evasion, stress-survival signaling, metabolic adaptability, and tumor microenvironment remodeling. We also evaluate emerging strategies targeting lactate production and transport, lactylation-regulating enzymes, and functionally validated substrates, including their potential use in combination therapies. Finally, we discuss major barriers to clinical translation, including incomplete characterization of regulatory enzymes, limitations in site-specific lactylome mapping, insufficient causal validation, lack of clinically qualified biomarkers, tumor metabolic heterogeneity, and challenges in achieving therapeutic selectivity. Collectively, protein lactylation represents an emerging mechanistic framework for understanding cancer treatment adaptation and a potentially targetable axis whose clinical relevance requires rigorous validation.

items.title: Nanocatalytic Immunotherapy Targeting Tumor-Resident Intracellular Bacteria for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Treatment and Metastasis Suppression.
items.abstract: Tumor-resident intracellular bacteria (TRIB) are prevalent within triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). As integral components of the tumor pathological microenvironment, TRIB accelerate TNBC development by regulating cell proliferation, metabolism and immunosuppression. They also enhance the resistance of circulating tumor cells to mechanical stress through cytoskeletal rearrangement, boosting tumor metastasis and hindering clinical therapy. This work develops an advanced TRIB-targeted therapeutic strategy to block TNBC progression by eliminating tumor cells and intracellular bacteria, remodeling tumor immunity and suppressing metastatic colonization. We fabricate cancer cell membrane-modified narrow-bandgap FeSe 2 nanosheets for enhanced ultrasound-triggered reactive oxygen species production and image-guided precise treatment. Such nanoplatforms utilize endogenous H 2 O 2 and GSH to amplify chemodynamic effects, induce severe oxidative stress and ferroptosis in tumor cells. Combined damage-associated and pathogen-associated molecular patterns efficiently activate dendritic cells and initiate robust antigen-specific T-cell immune responses. This study provides an alternative and promising strategy for the treatment of clinically metastatic breast cancer through intratumoral microbiota intervention.

items.title: Ultrasound-Activated Ce(IV)-Integrated Biomimetic Nanoplatform for Oxygenation-Reinforced Gas-Sonodynamic Ferroptosis and cGAS-STING-Driven Antitumor Immunity.
items.abstract: Immunologically "cold" tumors remain poorly responsive to immunotherapy because hypoxia-limited oxidative therapy, insufficient immunogenic tumor-cell death, and dysfunctional T-cell responses restrict the transition from local tumor destruction to systemic antitumor immunity. Here, an ultrasound-responsive Ce(IV)-integrated biomimetic nanoplatform, TcEM@Ce-P4CO@M, is developed to address these barriers. Ce 4+ /Ce 3+ redox cycling promotes H 2 O 2 decomposition and O 2 generation, sustaining ultrasound-triggered reactive oxygen species production under hypoxic conditions. Concurrently, P4CO-derived carbon monoxide contributes to mitochondrial oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. Endogenous iron-homeostasis remodeling and impairment of the SLC7A11/glutathione (GSH)/glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) antioxidant defense further favor ferroptosis-associated tumor-cell injury. Mitochondrial dysfunction and DNA damage are accompanied by enhanced stimulator of interferon genes (STING)-associated signaling, while co-delivered MSA-2 further reinforces STING-mediated innate immune activation, collectively contributing to an immunogenic environment that supports dendritic-cell maturation. The engineered tumor-derived membrane promotes tumor-associated delivery and provides CD86-mediated costimulation and anti-TIM-3-mediated checkpoint modulation. In 4T1 tumor models, this coordinated cascade suppresses primary tumors, inhibits non-irradiated distant tumors, reduces experimental pulmonary metastatic burden, and remodels the tumor immune microenvironment. Collectively, TcEM@Ce-P4CO@M converts hypoxia-limited local sonodynamic injury into ferroptosis-linked innate-to-adaptive systemic antitumor immunity.

items.title: Multilevel Determinants of Liver Cancer Screening Uptake in Community-Based High-Risk Populations in Chongqing, China: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Evidence on the uptake and determinants of liver cancer screening in Southwest China remains limited. This study aimed to assess the participation rate, influencing factors, and screening outcomes among high-risk individuals in a population-based liver cancer screening program. A community-based screening program was conducted across 18 districts or counties in Chongqing, China, from October 2013 to October 2022. High-risk individuals identified through a risk assessment system were invited to receive alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) testing and abdominal ultrasonography. A generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was applied to identify individual-level and structural factors associated with screening uptake. Reasons for non-participation and liver cancer detection rates were also assessed. Among the 369,393 individuals who completed the risk assessment, 37,381 were identified as being at high-risk for liver cancer. After exclusions, 34,647 were included in the final analysis. Of these, 14,062 underwent screening, yielding an uptake rate of 40.59%. Screening participation was significantly associated with younger age, occupational exposures, alcohol consumption, lower levels of physical activity, hepatitis B infection, history of liver cirrhosis, comorbidities, and family history of liver cancer. At the structural level, developed status, use of multiple mobilization strategies, and receiving allowances were positively associated with uptake. Among 20,585 non-participants, the most frequently reported barriers included no symptoms (93.61%), fear of diagnosis (92.60%), and lack of knowledge about cancer prevention and treatment (89.30%). Liver cancer was detected in 14 of the screened individuals, corresponding to a detection rate of 0.10%. Participation in liver cancer screening is shaped by a combination of individual and structural factors. Targeted interventions addressing key barriers (such as low risk perception, fear, and knowledge gaps) and structural factors (such as diversified mobilization and financial incentives) may help improve screening uptake among the high-risk populations. There is limited information about how well liver cancer screening works for people living in Southwest China. We wanted to find out how many high-risk people took part in local liver cancer screening, what factors influenced their decision to participate, and how many liver cancers were found through the program. We studied a community-based screening program covering 18 districts or counties in Chongqing between 2013 and 2022. People at high risk of liver cancer were invited to receive AFP testing and abdominal ultrasound scans. Only around 4 out of 10 high-risk people attended the screening. Participation was higher among younger people, and among those with hepatitis B, liver cirrhosis, a family history of liver cancer, alcohol consumption, occupational exposure to hazards, or multiple comorbidities. People in developed areas, people contacted through multiple mobilization methods, and people who received financial allowances were also more likely to attend. Most people who skipped screening said they had no symptoms, feared being diagnosed, or lacked knowledge about cancer prevention. Among those screened, only 0.10% were diagnosed with liver cancer. Both personal health conditions and structural conditions influence screening attendance. Future efforts should improve risk awareness, reduce fear of diagnosis, and spread health knowledge, while implementing community-level incentives, to increase screening uptake among high-risk residents,which may help find liver cancer at an earlier, more treatable stage.

items.title: Infectious Disease Screening in Hematopoietic Cell Donors: Risk Assessment, Regulation, and Selective Donor Utilization.
items.abstract: Donor-derived infections in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are uncommon but potentially severe complications that remain largely preventable through rigorous donor screening and risk mitigation strategies. Although reported incidence appears low, donor-derived infections are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality when transmission occurs in profoundly immunocompromised recipients. In the United States, donor eligibility is governed by Food and Drug Administration requirements for screening and testing for relevant communicable disease agents and diseases. European and international frameworks similarly require comprehensive donor evaluation and testing for major transmissible infections, with additional testing guided by epidemiologic and exposure risk. A key challenge across jurisdictions is distinguishing regulatory donor eligibility from clinical donor suitability and determining when individualized donor-recipient risk assessment is appropriate. Advances in nucleic acid testing have markedly shortened diagnostic window periods for blood-borne pathogens. Concurrently, highly effective antiviral therapies, particularly for hepatitis B and hepatitis C, have transformed select historically prohibitive infections into increasingly manageable risks. These developments have supported selective clinical consideration of donors who remain ineligible under traditional regulatory criteria when an applicable regulatory pathway permits use. This review examines pathogen-specific transmission risk, contemporary screening strategies, and evolving approaches to donor eligibility in HCT. Future donor screening frameworks will likely evolve toward adaptive, pathogen-specific models that integrate molecular diagnostics, recipient mitigation strategies, and real-world transplant outcomes to optimize both safety and donor access.

items.title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with MASLD: A translational study.
items.abstract: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, potentially involving systemic metabolic dysfunction and cardiac remodeling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve metabolic dysfunction in MASLD; however, their associations with cardiovascular outcomes and effects on MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. In this translational study, we integrated a real-world TriNetX cohort of patients with MASLD and T2D with complementary experimental studies in a mouse model of MASLD. Following propensity score matching, 42,910 patients were included in each treatment group. GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite cardiovascular outcome compared with sulfonylurea therapy (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% confidence interval 0.84-0.91; P < 0.001), although this association was not statistically significant in 90-day and 180-day landmark analyses. In Western diet-fed mice, GLP-1 RA treatment improved selected indices of cardiac function and attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Although myocardial fibrosis was numerically reduced, the difference compared with vehicle-treated mice was not statistically significant (P = 0.28). Molecular analyses showed reduced expression of fibrosis- and extracellular matrix remodeling-related markers, including CTGF, TGF-β1, and vimentin. Collectively, GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the primary observational analysis, although this finding was not consistently supported by sensitivity analyses. Complementary experimental findings suggest improvements in selected cardiac functional indices and changes in fibrosis-associated molecular remodeling, warranting further investigation.

items.title: Pneumococcal vaccine after hematopoietic cell transplantation: a rapid review of four-dose pneumococcal conjugate vaccine schedules.
items.abstract: Hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients are at substantially elevated risk for invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) due to prolonged immunocompromised state, yet optimal pneumococcal vaccine product selection and scheduling, including the role of higher-valency pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs), have not undergone Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices review. We conducted a rapid review to synthesize evidence on the immunogenicity and safety of four-dose PCV schedules in HCT recipients to inform future clinical guidance. Following Cochrane rapid review methods and PRISMA guidelines, we searched Medline, Embase, and Scopus (initial: November 2024; updated: March 2025) and identified 31 eligible studies. Four studies directly evaluated four-dose PCV13 or PCV15 regimens in allogeneic HCT recipients, and only one study provided a direct randomized comparison. Among studies that allowed comparison, four-dose PCV13 schedules consistently generated higher overall and serotype-specific IgG and opsonophagocytic activity responses than three-dose PCV13 followed by 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23), while PPSV23 provided limited additional benefit when administered within 1-2 months of the final PCV13 dose. Both randomized and nonrandomized studies demonstrated robust antibody responses following the fourth PCV dose, and safety profiles were acceptable. Although adverse events were more frequent after the fourth PCV dose, serious vaccine-related events were rare and difficult to attribute given underlying comorbidities. Findings from 27 supporting studies further contextualized optimal timing and product choice, showing that later initiation (≥6 months post-HCT) was often associated with stronger and more durable immune responses, although waning immunity remained common. PCV-based regimens were consistently more immunogenic than PPSV23-only schedules. No studies evaluated PCV20 or PCV21 in HCT recipients, representing a major evidence gap despite their expanded serotype coverage. Overall, the available evidence provides evidence of immunogenicity and safety with a four-dose PCV-based schedule initiated 3-6 months post-HCT, while critical research gaps remain regarding higher-valency PCVs, mixed-product schedules, and strategies tailored to transplant type or individual immunologic risk.

items.title: Predictors of Incident Hepatic Fibrosis and Steatotic Liver Disease-Associated Fibrosis Among Women with and without HIV.
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis is an important cause of non-AIDS morbidity among women with HIV (WWH), but predictors of incident fibrosis in the absence of viral hepatitis are not well defined. We included women with and without HIV enrolled in the Women's Interagency HIV Study (WIHS), now part of the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study, who underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) between 2013 and 2020 as part of the Liver Disease and Reproductive Aging (LIVRA) Study and had at least two VCTE exams. Participants with viral hepatitis, heavy alcohol use, or baseline fibrosis were excluded. Poisson regression estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for incident fibrosis, defined as liver stiffness ≥7.1 kPa. Models included time-updated covariates and tested interactions between HIV and steatosis measured by controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Among 1,036 women (709 WWH, 327 without HIV), median age was 49 years and median BMI 32 kg/m2. Over a mean follow-up of 3.5 years, 19% developed incident fibrosis. HIV infection (IRR 1.72, 95% CI 1.12-2.65) and higher CAP (per 10 dB/m; IRR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00-1.08) were associated with fibrosis in multivariable adjusted models. The association between CAP and fibrosis differed by HIV status (interaction p = 0.02) and was attenuated among WWH. Fibrosis without steatosis accounted for 28% of new fibrosis in WWH and was more common in those with prior AIDS. HIV infection predicted incident hepatic fibrosis, while steatosis was a weaker predictor in WWH. Fibrosis without steatosis was common, suggesting distinct fibrosis phenotypes and potential HIV-specific pathways of liver injury.

items.title: The State of Health in Jordan, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study.
items.abstract: Jordan's health system has evolved amid rapid urbanization and the strain of hosting one of the world's largest refugee populations per capita. This study comprehensively evaluates national disease burden trends in Jordan from 1990 to 2023 to inform health priorities. Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 framework, we analyzed age-standardized rates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) across 370 diseases and 88 risk factors. Data were derived from national censuses, health surveys, disease registries, and hospital records, and harmonized using standardized GBD modeling and estimation procedures. Analyses were stratified by age, sex, and cause. Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized DALYs declined by 33.88% (95% UI: -37.38 to -30.59), with greater reductions in males (-38.83%; -42.22 to -35.60) than females (-27.22%; -31.33 to -23.58). YLLs decreased by 49.38% (-50.93 to -47.68), while YLDs remained comparatively stable (2.49%; -2.37 to 7.47). Using mutually exclusive GBD Level 3 causes, ischemic heart disease and diabetes mellitus were the two leading causes of DALYs in 2023. Diabetes mellitus rose from 7th place in 1990 to 2nd place in 2023, while neonatal disorders declined from 1st to 7th place. Metabolic risks remained important contributors to the overall disease burden. Jordan's age-standardized diabetes DALY rate in 2023 was approximately 1.56 times the global rate. Jordan's health profile has shifted toward a greater burden from noncommunicable diseases, while age-standardized health loss and premature mortality have declined substantially. In contrast, nonfatal disability changed comparatively little. These findings provide an evidence base for primary prevention of NCDs and for long-term strategies addressing the country's evolving health challenges.

items.title: Claudin-12-Expressing Fibroblasts Facilitate Metastatic Spread of Pancreatic Cancer Through Physical Interactions.
items.abstract: Claudins (CLDNs), as major components of tight junctions in epithelial cells, are emerging as attractive non-mutant targets for controlling the growth and metastasis of various cancers. However, the mechanisms by which CLDNs modulate tumor progression remain largely unclear. Here, we unexpectedly found that CLDN12 is expressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which are generally not considered tight junction-forming cells. CLDN12 expression in fibroblasts increased their motility and, importantly, promoted direct adhesion to pancreatic cancer cells through homophilic CLDN12-CLDN12 interactions. This CLDN12-dependent physical interaction between fibroblasts and tumor cells markedly enhanced cancer cell invasion. Moreover, TGF-β produced by cancer cells further induced the upregulation of CLDN12 expression in fibroblasts. In vivo, CLDN12-positive fibroblasts facilitated distant metastasis of pancreatic cancer to liver and diaphragm. Targeting CLDN12 with the synthetic peptide C12-pm efficiently decreased the liver metastasis of pancreatic cancer. Taken together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized role of CLDN12-expressing fibroblasts in promoting pancreatic cancer metastasis through direct physical interactions with tumor cells and highlight CLDN12-mediated interactions as a potential therapeutic target for metastatic pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Anastrozole-Induced Liver Injury: A Pooled Analysis of 11 Published Case Reports.
items.abstract: Anastrozole, a first-line adjuvant treatment for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, is generally well-tolerated but has been rarely associated with idiosyncratic liver injury. This brief report pooled and retrospectively analyzed 11 published case reports from PubMed and Web of Science. All identified patients were female, with a mean age of 70, suggesting that most reported cases were elderly white women. The latency period from drug initiation to injury was highly variable, ranging from days to years. Laboratory findings primarily indicated a hepatocellular pattern of injury, and most patients had no significant imaging abnormalities. Critically, discontinuation of anastrozole was the cornerstone of management, leading to recovery in 90% of cases, although one fatal outcome was reported. This analysis underscores that while rare, anastrozole-induced liver injury can be severe. Clinicians should be aware of this potential toxicity, monitor liver function appropriately, and discontinue the drug promptly if injury is suspected. Unfortunately, these findings are limited by the small sample size and publication bias inherent to case-report-based analyses. Further research is needed to understand the underlying mechanisms and risk factors.

items.title: Association between antibiotic exposure and survival outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are frequently exposed to antibiotics. This study aims to evaluate the impact of antibiotic use on the survival outcomes of HCC patients treated with ICIs. This study followed the PRISMA guidelines and systematically retrieved literature from PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases up to August 7, 2026. Studies comparing the clinical outcomes (overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and disease control rate (DCR)) of HCC patients receiving ICI treatment with and without antibiotic exposure were included. The quality of the studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Before conducting the meta-analysis, the original hazard ratios (HRs)/odd ratios (ORs) and their 95% CIs were log-transformed to achieve a normal distribution. Statistical analysis was performed using Stata 15 software, and pooled HRs/ORs with 95% CIs were calculated. A total of 12 retrospective cohort studies were included, involving 3,643 patients (761 exposed to antibiotics). The results showed that the median OS of the antibiotic-exposed group (12.2 months) was shorter than that of the non-exposed group (17.0 months). The meta-analysis indicated that antibiotic use was significantly associated with poorer OS (HR = 1.29, 95% CI [1.17-1.41]). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the OS finding. In terms of PFS, the median PFS of the antibiotic-exposed group (5.2 months) was shorter than that of the non-exposed group (7.5 months), and antibiotic use was also significantly associated with poorer PFS (HR = 1.27, 95% CI [1.01-1.59]), although this association was not robust in sensitivity analyses. The analyses of ORR and DCR did not show significant differences between the groups. No significant publication bias was detected on the basis of visual inspection of funnel plots and Egger's and Begg's tests. For HCC patients receiving ICI therapy, antibiotic exposure was significantly associated with reduced OS. A significant association with poorer PFS was also observed, although this finding was not robust in sensitivity analyses and should therefore be interpreted with caution. No statistically significant differences were observed for ORR or DCR.
